mutant.description: The governing order names no mutant, so none is owed and none was run; this states that rather than letting the absence read as a pass. What stands in its place is stronger for a deploy: a BEFORE/AFTER pair on every read that matters, taken with the same instrument on the same host. admin_fabric.py and its roster were ABSENT live on three separate pre-act reads and present with a matching md5 after; the new route did not exist and returns 401 after; the MCP tool surface was enumerated by name before and after; the rollback artifact was content-verified before the act and re-read as intact and distinct from `latest` after it.
mutant.expected: n/a -- the spec names no mutant.
mutant.observed: Every before/after pair moved only where this act should move it: admin_fabric absent -> present at the build input's md5; route absent -> 401 owner-gated; MainPID 862375 -> 864717; latest -> the release artifact; tool surface 66 -> 66 with an EMPTY name difference; .env TRANSCRIPT_MEETING_ALLOWLIST non-empty both before and after, so OG-tl-1 was preserved rather than reverted.

determinism.method: The cold read was sampled SEVEN times across two bases and three wall-clock points (four on 91811b648a at ~14:0xZ, three on c97232408d at ~15:5xZ, plus AC3's own at ~16:2xZ), each in a fresh interpreter so each cache was empty by construction. The census was run twice, once per base. The tool surface was read three times (twice before on each base, once after). /health and the route were read by the deploy's own read-back and again by an independent SSM invocation. AC1/AC2/AC3 were each run once post-close, and AC2's logic additionally re-run from the main tree.
determinism.observed: Stable where the world was stable and directional where this cell moved it. The ONE quantity that was NOT stable is the cold read, and its instability is a real property of the system rather than instrument noise: it tracks a rolling 6-hour record count that grew ~3,150 -> 4,040 during this cell's execution, carrying the cold time 13.6 s -> 24.4 s. A single sample against a fixed 30 s bar would therefore have certified only the moment it was taken, which is precisely why seven were taken and why the trend is filed as a row.

declared_exclusions.item: The recorded base 91811b648a, the release branch cut from it, and its artifacts.
declared_exclusions.reason: Discarded, not reused. The issuer held the act (msg 32796) so OG-ap-4/OG-tl-1 could go first; the live base then moved to c97232408d. Step 1 requires reading deployed_commit AT THE ACT, so the old branch was deleted and the tree re-cut, and the census, cold read, rollback target and tool-surface BEFORE were all re-taken. Keeping the old base would have done real harm, not merely been stale: the pre-OG-tl-1 deploy script hardcodes TRANSCRIPT_MEETING_ALLOWLIST= (EMPTY) in the rendered .env, and the .env is RENDERED rather than merged, so it would have silently reverted a cell that landed 15 minutes earlier -- while this cell's blast radius claims 'no .env key'.
